headline: GOLDSEEK: SILVER 'PERHAPS SOMEWHAT UNDERPRICED' AS GOLD/SILVER RATIO TOPS 73X — KEY SUPPORT ZONE IN FOCUS
snippet: In a GoldSeek column published October 18, analyst Mark Mead Baillie argues that silver is perhaps somewhat underpriced at the current gold/silver ratio of approximately 73x — the widest divergence since early 2026 — and that gold is basing against its short-term trend. The piece notes silver closed near $57/oz Friday, still approximately 54% below its 2026 cycle high near $121/oz, while gold holds the $4,100 support zone. Baillie identifies a critical weekly support band for silver that must hold to form a higher low above the July bottom at $54.77/oz. The analysis is a useful data point for retail investors weighing silver-focused junior miners: at 73x gold, silver's underperformance relative to gold is extreme by historical standards, and ratio extremes of 70-75x have historically preceded significant silver catch-up moves. However, the FOMC meeting on October 27-28 remains the near-term wildcard — a rate hike surprise could reprice silver's industrial demand assumptions and extend the divergence further before the ratio mean-reverts.

headline: CRUX INVESTOR: SSR'S $464M ROXMORE DEAL EXPOSES DWINDLING NEVADA GOLD INVENTORY — M&A PREMIUMS TO ACCELERATE
snippet: A Crux Investor analysis published October 17 examines SSR Mining's C$712 million acquisition of Roxmore Resources and its 5.2-million-ounce Converse gold project in Nevada — framing it as a symptom of a broader problem: high-quality, permitted gold assets in safe jurisdictions are running out, and producers are paying up for proximity to existing infrastructure. SSR's deal values the 2.2 Moz Indicated / 3.0 Moz Inferred Converse project at roughly C$6.75 per share cash plus a new SpinCo holding Roxmore's exploration assets, representing a 27% premium to the October 9 closing price. The analysis argues this is the type of near-mine consolidation play that produces the highest returns for acquirers — Converse sits six kilometres from SSR's Marigold complex, enabling shared infrastructure and a targeted 150,000-170,000 oz/year production addition by 2033. For junior exploration investors, the deal signals that the major and mid-tier producers most at risk of reserve replacement are actively scanning for developed-but-unbuilt assets in Nevada, BC, Ontario and Quebec — making advanced-stage explorers with permitted or near-permit gold deposits in those jurisdictions logical takeout candidates in the current cycle.

headline: GOLD 'STUCK' IN $4,100-$4,200 RANGE ON SUNDAY — ALL EYES ON OCT 27-28 FOMC AS KEY BREAKOUT CATALYST
snippet: Spot gold is trading around $4,165-$4,179/oz on Sunday October 18, consolidating within the same $4,100-$4,200 range that has capped both dips and rallies for the past two weeks, according to Kitco-sourced market data cited by Vietnam.vn. The 'stuck' characterization reflects the stalemate between gold's structural bull drivers (central bank buying, ETF accumulation at four-year highs, geopolitical safe-haven demand) and the near-term headwind of elevated Fed rate-hike probability around the October 27-28 FOMC meeting. With hike odds now at roughly 29% following Fed Chair Warsh's IMF comments Friday — down from 70% midweek — the range is likely to hold through the weekend before any directional move. For junior mining equity investors, range-bound gold at $4,165 still represents historically elevated valuations supportive of junior explorer net asset values, even as mining stocks have corrected 35-40% from 2026 cycle highs on cost inflation and rate-hike fears. A sustained break above $4,200 heading into the FOMC meeting would likely trigger a repricing of gold equity valuations.

headline: FREEGOLD DRILLS 213M AT 1.24 G/T GOLD AT ALASKA'S GOLDEN SUMMIT — 58,000M 2026 SEASON FEEDS 2027 PFS
snippet: Freegold Ventures (TSX-V: FVL) reported October 16 that drilling at its Golden Summit project in Alaska returned a 213-metre interval grading 1.24 g/t gold in the Dolphin area, including a higher-grade sub-interval of 21 metres at 5.77 g/t gold. The company has completed more than 58,000 metres of drilling at Golden Summit in 2026 — with the program continuing through mid-December — and plans to incorporate all 2026 results alongside approximately 40,000 metres drilled in 2025 into an updated resource estimate that will form the foundation for a 2027 preliminary feasibility study. The current Golden Summit resource stands at 17.2 Moz Indicated at 1.24 g/t gold and 11.9 Moz Inferred at 1.04 g/t gold — a substantial base for PFS-level mine planning. For investors in Alaskan gold development stories, Golden Summit's combination of bulk-tonnage scale, multi-year consistent drilling results, and a defined PFS timeline represents one of the few advancing development-stage gold projects in North America with a clear catalytic pathway to resource refinement and economic study completion in 2027.

headline: GOLD FUTURES RALLY 2% TO $4,191 AS AI TECH SELLOFF LIFTS HAVEN DEMAND — ASX GOLD PRODUCERS EVOLUTION, NEWMONT BENEFIT
snippet: Gold futures rose approximately 2% to around US$4,191.50/oz on October 16 as a CoreWeave-led AI and technology stock selloff drove investors toward precious metals safe-havens, with 10-year Treasury yields retreating to 5.08%. Australian gold producers benefited directly: Evolution Mining and Newmont's ASX-listed shares moved higher alongside spot gold's intraday recovery, providing a glimpse of the leverage that ASX-listed gold miners carry to each swing in gold price. The October 16 rally came after a midweek correction to $4,098 following the hot September CPI print — making the full-week price action instructive for junior mining investors: the $4,100 support zone held, and gold's recovery to $4,165-$4,179 by end of week was driven by both the Fed's pivot messaging and haven flows from the AI sector selloff. The ASX market note is a reminder that institutional investors in Australian gold producers are actively managing gold price exposure, and that sharp tech selloffs — increasingly common in 2026 — have had a consistent positive secondary effect on gold equity prices.

headline: BONTERRA BARRY GOLD PEA RETURNS C$665M AFTER-TAX NPV AT $3,500/OZ — 14X JUMP FROM 2022 STUDY WITH GOLD FIELDS EARNING IN
snippet: Bonterra Resources (TSX-V: BTR) released a new independent Preliminary Economic Assessment on its Barry open pit and underground project in Quebec's Urban-Barry gold camp on October 14, reporting an after-tax NPV of C$665 million and a 54% IRR at a conservative US$3,500/oz long-term gold price — with the NPV rising to C$976 million and the IRR to 77% at spot gold of US$4,100/oz. The study, prepared by BBA Consultants under NI 43-101, is a 13.8x improvement over the C$48.3 million NPV in the 2022 PEA — driven by a larger resource base, updated mine plan and a dramatically higher gold price environment. The plan uses only approximately 40% of the February 2026 mineral resource estimate, leaving significant upside from potential resource expansion. Gold Fields is earning into the project by committing C$30 million in work expenditures before November 2026 — bringing institutional validation and funded exploration. For junior gold investors in Quebec, the Barry PEA is a significant datapoint: it demonstrates that Canadian open-pit gold projects with large resource bases can generate exceptional economics at current gold prices, and that farm-in structures with major miners are one effective route to funded development for early-stage developers.

headline: GOLDSEEK: GOLD CORRECTION IS SETUP FOR RALLY TO $5,400 — SECULAR BULL INTACT DESPITE SHORT-TERM WEAKNESS
snippet: GoldSeek analyst Stewart Thomson published an October 14 piece arguing that gold's current correction — which has seen the metal and gold equities pull back significantly from 2026 highs — is the setup for the next major leg higher, with a target of $5,400/oz. Thomson's thesis distinguishes between the short-term technical weakness (driven by Fed rate-hike fears and seasonal patterns) and the secular bull market structural drivers (central bank accumulation, de-dollarization, safe-haven demand, and supply constraints). At $4,165/oz with the October 27-28 FOMC meeting as the key near-term inflection point, Thomson's framework places gold in a basing pattern consistent with prior bull market corrections that preceded sharp moves higher. For retail junior mining investors, the $5,400 target represents roughly 30% upside from current levels — which, with typical 3-5x leverage in junior explorer equities relative to the gold price, could imply substantial rerating of quality junior names if the thesis plays out. The caveat: a rate hike at the October FOMC meeting would likely delay the next leg and could test the $4,100 support level before any rally materialises.

headline: EQUINOX GOLD Q3 PRODUCTION SURGES 34% TO 237,019 OZ AS ORLA ASSETS ADD MUSSELWHITE AND CAMINO ROJO
snippet: Equinox Gold (TSX: EQX) reported October 13 that Q3 2026 gold production reached 237,019 ounces — a 34% year-over-year increase — following the July 31 closing of its combination with Orla Mining, which added Musselwhite (Ontario) and Camino Rojo (Mexico) to the portfolio. Year-to-date production of 611,483 oz puts the company on track for its 2026 guidance of 870,000-920,000 oz, or approximately 1.1 million oz including Orla's full-year contribution. The company's South Railroad project in Nevada received its Record of Decision and final federal permits during Q3, targeting first gold production in 2028. About $190 million of debt was repaid during the quarter, leaving $365 million drawn on the revolving credit facility. For junior mining investors, Equinox's Q3 results illustrate how mid-tier producer consolidation through accretive acquisitions can rapidly re-rate a company toward million-ounce producer status — a scale threshold that typically commands meaningfully higher price-to-NAV multiples from institutional investors and opens access to index inclusion and broader capital market visibility.

headline: SSR MINING TO ACQUIRE ROXMORE RESOURCES FOR $464M CASH — 5.2 MOZ CONVERSE GOLD PROJECT ADJACENT TO MARIGOLD
snippet: SSR Mining (TSX: SSRM) announced October 13 it has reached a definitive agreement to acquire all outstanding shares of Roxmore Resources (TSX: RM) for C$6.75 per share in cash — a 27% premium to Roxmore's October 9 closing price — plus shares of a newly created SpinCo holding Roxmore's non-core Rattlesnake Hills, Shabu River and Newton exploration assets. The total transaction value is approximately C$712 million (roughly US$498 million). The core asset being acquired is the Converse gold project in Nevada, located six kilometres west of SSR's existing Marigold mine complex, with a 2026 resource of 2.2 Moz Indicated and 3.0 Moz Inferred gold. SSR targets adding 150,000-170,000 oz/year at Converse, with initial construction capital of $800-900 million and first production in 2033. The deal will be funded from cash on hand; closing is targeted for Q4 2026 subject to Roxmore shareholder, court and regulatory approvals. The acquisition represents a classic near-mine consolidation play — avoiding greenfield exploration risk by buying a delineated, adjacent resource that benefits from SSR's existing Nevada operational platform.

headline: EXCELSIOR: RESOURCE INVESTORS ENDURING PRESSURE COOKER — SILJ HOLDS 50-WEEK SUPPORT, CAPITULATION SIGNAL WATCH
snippet: An October 18 Excelsior Prosperity commentary describes a rough week for resource stock investors, with metals equities falling through the middle of the week on hot CPI and Fed rate-hike fears before a Friday partial recovery. The key technical level highlighted is the Amplify Junior Silver Miners ETF (SILJ), which closed Friday just below its 50-week moving average near $27.25 — a level the analyst identifies as a critical support zone that, if held, would preserve the case for a sustained junior miners recovery. The piece addresses the psychological dimension of investing in junior resource stocks during prolonged underperformance: how retail investors experience the 'pressure cooker' of watching the underlying commodity (gold near $4,165/oz) hold near record levels while their equity positions remain deeply underwater relative to cycle highs. For TSX-V and ASX-listed junior mining investors, the SILJ support level is a useful proxy indicator: the ETF's relative positioning against its moving average is a sector-level signal that institutional flows are either stabilising or still in distribution mode, which typically precedes either a capitulation bottom or extended base-building.

headline: IAEA: GLOBAL NUCLEAR EXPANSION FACES URANIUM SUPPLY CHALLENGE AS EXISTING MINES DECLINE — NEW PRODUCTION URGENTLY NEEDED
snippet: The IAEA's Nuclear Technology Review 2026, reported October 18, warns that production from existing uranium mines is projected to decline sharply while nuclear fuel demand rises — requiring new and expanded mines, and reopened idled operations, to avoid a supply crunch. The IAEA now projects 641 to 1,045 GW of global nuclear capacity by 2050, up from its 2025 assessment of 561-992 GW, reflecting accelerating new reactor commitments from Europe, Asia, and North America. A companion OECD-NEA/IAEA Red Book analysis projects an annual mine output gap of 46,000 tonnes below reactor requirements under a high-demand scenario by 2040 — equivalent to 41% of projected annual needs unmet by the current assessed pipeline. For junior uranium explorers on the TSX-V and CSE, the IAEA's updated capacity projections validate the structural demand case while simultaneously underscoring the supply challenge: existing mines cannot service the growth in demand, and new projects require 10-15 years of development lead time. With long-term uranium contracts at $96-97/lb — an 18-year high — the economics of advancing new uranium projects are as strong as they have been in two decades.
